title: Build an AI Job Search Assistant with Google Sheets
summary: Find jobs at companies you choose, check the actual requirements, and save a shortlist to Google Sheets. Includes a template, prompts and Action recipes.
body_markdown:
An **AI job search assistant** can check a company’s current openings, explain how a posting fits your preferences, and save the roles you choose to **Google Sheets** . You will build **Shortlist Desk** , a personal assistant that keeps the reason for your interest beside the original job link.


Imagine your search is fairly specific: backend engineering, London or UK remote, and a chance to use your Python experience. You already know one company you would like to join. The useful next step is finding a role worth reading closely, then remembering both its appeal and its compromises.


The goal: one role with its original link and the tradeoff you approved, saved in Google Sheets. The real saved row is paired with Quickchat AI's confirmation.


The example follows[Monzo’s Backend Engineer III posting](https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/monzo/jobs/6635595) . It allows London or UK-remote work, while its application code is primarily Go. That makes it a useful near match for our fictional reader: a location fit with a language tradeoff, rather than an invented “perfect match.” Openings change; the source was checked on **17 November 2026** .


The Google connection, saved row and save conversation were captured from the connected test Agent. Configuration screenshots use a local copy of the same setup.


[Download the Shortlist Desk starter kit](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/shortlist-desk-kit.zip) . It includes the spreadsheet header, four complete Action recipes, the Main Prompt and a test checklist. Use the files as copyable settings, not as an automatic import.


Follow the steps tochoose your criteria ,create the assistant ,read current jobs ,check the fit ,connect your shortlist , andsave and verify a role .


## Step 1: Which companies and jobs do you want to track?


Start with one employer and a short set of preferences. A small, explicit search is easier to inspect than a long list of vaguely relevant vacancies.


1. Open the employer’s careers page and follow its job links. For this example, use[Monzo’s public Greenhouse board](https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/monzo) . The board token is` monzo` .
2. Write down your role, location and work preferences. Our reader wants individual-contributor backend work, London or explicitly UK-remote, with Python experience relevant to the discussion.
3. Separate requirements from preferences. If Python must be the main production language, say so. If you would learn Go for the right role, say that instead.


Decide which criteria rule a job out and which start a conversation. These are fictional search preferences, not an assessment of a real applicant.


You do not need a CV for this build. The assistant compares your stated preferences with the posting; it does not decide whether you are qualified or eligible to work in a country.


## Step 2: How do you create your AI job search assistant?


Create a Quickchat AI Agent and give it one job: inspect configured company boards and help you keep a personal shortlist.


1. [Create a Quickchat AI account](https://app.quickchat.ai/register) and open your Agent.
2. Under **Identity** , name it **Shortlist Desk** . Paste` main-prompt.txt` from the kit into **Main Prompt** and save.
3. Keep this personal workflow in the authenticated dashboard’s **AI Preview** . Under **Your Website → Install → Availability and access** , turn **Widget & Embed access** off and set **Chat Page Access** to **Nobody** . Anyone who can reach an Agent with a Sheet-reading Action could ask it about that Sheet.


The Main Prompt sets the decision rules. The Actions you add next give the assistant access to current evidence.


The prompt makes three distinctions: **posting evidence versus inference** , **proposing a save versus confirming it** , and **saved versus applied** . Those distinctions will matter more than giving the assistant a job-hunting personality.


## Step 3: How do you read a company’s current job openings?


Use two read-only Actions: one lists the employer’s jobs, and the other reads a selected posting. Greenhouse’s[Job Board API](https://docs.greenhouse.io/job-board.html) allows these public GET requests without an API key.


Open **Actions & MCPs → Add Action → API Action** . Create the two Actions below, using the kit’s exact descriptions. The[API Action builder guide](https://quickchat.ai/post/connect-ai-agent-to-any-api) explains the editor and its plain-English builder.


Editor field Action 1 Action 2


API Action Name` List Monzo jobs`` Read selected job`


Method` GET`` GET`


What to ask the user first No parameters Required Text parameter` job_id`


Headers` Accept: application/json`` Accept: application/json`


Body Empty Empty


In **API Endpoint** , use these URLs respectively:


```text
https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/monzo/jobs
https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/monzo/jobs/{{job_id}}
```


For the detail Action, set the` job_id` description to: “The exact job ID returned by List Monzo jobs and Read selected job. Never invent an ID.” Insert the parameter through **Add AI Data** so it becomes a variable chip in the URL.


First, get titles, locations, IDs and original links from the fixed board.


Then use a returned posting ID to read the description behind a candidate.


Keep each response available to the Agent. The list’s` meta.total` lets you check coverage;` job_id` comes from the posting’s` id` , not` internal_job_id` . Fetch compact listings first, then descriptions only for the roles you discuss. If the returned list is incomplete or too large to process, report that limit instead of calling it a complete search.


Activate both read Actions. In **AI Preview** , send:


```text
I work mainly in Python and want an individual-contributor backend role in London or explicitly UK remote. Check current Monzo jobs and explain the fit and any gaps for Backend Engineer III. Keep it concise.
```


## Step 4: How can the assistant explain whether a role fits?


A useful match explanation pairs each claim with something the employer actually wrote. Open the original posting alongside the assistant’s answer and check the location, responsibilities and requirements yourself.


Compare both sides of the answer. A role can fit your location and interests while still asking you to learn another language.


For the example role, **London or Remote (UK)** supports our location preference. The posting’s description of Go as its main application language means the assistant should not call this a Python role. If Python is non-negotiable, ask it to exclude the role. If you are open to Go, keep that tradeoff in the note you save.


Try a second question:


```text
Does UK remote mean I can do this job while living in Spain? Use only what this posting says.
```


The expected answer distinguishes remote work within the UK from permission to work abroad. Silence about a country is not permission. The same rule applies to salary and sponsorship: use an explicit statement or leave the answer unknown.


This is also your first tuning loop. If an answer overstates a fit, inspect the called detail Action in **Inbox** , identify the unsupported sentence, tighten the Action’s description, and rerun the same question. Change one instruction at a time so you can tell what helped.


## Step 5: How do you connect a job shortlist to Google Sheets?


Connect Google Sheets after the assistant can find and explain a role. The integration creates a spreadsheet and starter logging Action; you will add a **Shortlist** tab and two purpose-built Actions.


1. Open **Actions & MCPs → Add Action → Google Sheets → Connect** . Sign in to your Google account and approve the requested access.
2. Open the spreadsheet from the connection dialog. The integration uses per-file access, not unrestricted Drive access. The[Google Sheets connection guide](https://quickchat.ai/post/connect-ai-agent-to-google-sheets) explains this setup.
3. Disable the generated` log_lead_to_google_sheet` Action while configuring the shortlist. Leave its name intact; the connection uses it to find the starter.
4. Add a tab named exactly` Shortlist` . Paste` Shortlist.tsv` from the kit into cell A1. Freeze row 1, enable text wrapping, and give the title and match-note columns enough width to read. Keep all ten columns visible and in the supplied A:J order, with` source_key` in A1 and` checked_at` in J1.


Use the spreadsheet created by this connection. Copying an unrelated Sheet's ID into an Action does not grant access to it.


The ten columns keep the visible decision beside the identifiers needed to check it:


```text
source_key | company | job_id | title | location | job_url | status | match_note | source_updated_at | checked_at
```


Template diagram. The status starts as saved. Keep both the provider's update time and the time you checked the posting.


For the optional six-column reading view shown at the start, add a separate tab named` Saved roles` and paste the kit’s` saved-roles-view.txt` formula into A1. It displays the company, role, location, original link, status and match note. Edit statuses and notes in` Shortlist` ;` Saved roles` updates from that tab.


The optional Saved roles view shows the decision in six columns. Both Actions still read and write the ten-column Shortlist tab.


Create **Read my shortlist** and **Save selected role** using` action-recipes.json` in the kit. Find your spreadsheet ID inside the generated starter Action’s existing URL and copy it into both recipes in place of` APP_CREATED_SHEET_ID` . Keep that ID fixed in the editor.


Setting Read my shortlist Save selected role


Method` GET`` POST`


Range` Shortlist!A1:J501`` Shortlist!A:J:append`


Authorization header` Bearer {{google_sheets_access_token}}`` Bearer {{google_sheets_access_token}}`


Body Empty The kit’s one-row JSON body


Query parameters None` valueInputOption=RAW` ,` insertDataOption=INSERT_ROWS`


The read URL ends in` /values/Shortlist!A1:J501` . The save URL ends in` /values/Shortlist!A:J:append` . Both begin with` https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/` followed by the fixed spreadsheet ID. The save Action also needs` Content-Type: application/json` .


Read the existing source keys before proposing a new row.


Append only the selected posting and approved note. The kit supplies every parameter description.


The row key is` greenhouse:monzo:<job_id>` . The request fixes the company to` Monzo` and the status to` saved` ;` {{current_timestamp}}` supplies the check time in UTC. The model fills the returned job fields and your approved match note. Google documents the[read contract](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values/get) and[append contract](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values/append) .


After reviewing the settings, activate **Read my shortlist** and **Save selected role** . The POST Action stays inactive until you switch it on.


## Step 6: How do you save a role and check the result?


Saving is a short conversation with a visible checkpoint. The assistant reads the shortlist, proposes a role and note, and waits for a separate confirmation.


Send **“Save Backend Engineer III to my shortlist.”** Read the proposed note before approving it. It should retain the Go tradeoff, not flatten the role into a generic recommendation.


Review the decision you will want to remember later, not just the title.


Reply **“Confirm save with that match note.”** The prompt tells the assistant to recheck the posting and existing keys, append one row, then read the shortlist again.


The repeated read catches ordinary accidental repeats. It is not an atomic uniqueness guarantee if multiple conversations save simultaneously.


Inspect the result in two places:


1. In **Inbox** , expand the called Action. Check that` updates.updatedRange` spans columns A:J, such as` Shortlist!A2:J2` for the first saved row.
2. In your Google Sheet, inspect that exact row. Each value must sit under its matching header, from` source_key` in column A to` checked_at` in J. Verify the job ID, original URL and approved note. A successful reply alone is not proof that Google received the row.


Our first live check placed the row in B:K while edge columns were hidden. We made all ten columns visible and reran the same recipe; the row then aligned with A:J.


One confirmed save, followed by a readback. The append returned Shortlist!A2:J2, and the follow-up read found the same source key and approved note.


Ask to save the same role again. The assistant should find its exact key and keep one row. If a request times out, read before retrying. The recipe reads 500 data rows; expand its configured range before the shortlist reaches that limit.


A second confirmation found the existing source key. The Sheet still contained one saved row, and no second append ran.


You can later change` saved` to` applied` or add interview notes in the Sheet yourself. Applications still happen through the employer’s original link.


## Step 7: How do you test the assistant and add another company?


Test the decisions as well as the happy path. Use **Testing → Simulation** with the kit’s test messages, then inspect the corresponding Inbox calls. Simulation can execute active writes, so start with the save Action disabled and enable it only for your test Sheet.


Keep the same questions when you change a prompt. Check the actual Action result as well as the wording of the reply. Test What to verify


Ask for Python-only backend work A Go role is not presented as a Python match


Ask about remote work from Spain UK remote is not expanded to every country


Ask to save, without confirming No append occurs


Confirm, then repeat the save One matching source key remains


Posting disappears or Google access fails No invented current posting or successful save


To use a different Greenhouse employer, copy the kit and replace` monzo` in both Greenhouse URLs,` Monzo` in the save body’s company cell, and` greenhouse:monzo:` in the body, descriptions and Main Prompt. Update the employer references in the Action names and descriptions too. Verify that employer’s board token, then repeat the read, fit, confirmation and readback tests. Keep each copy tied to one fixed employer and its own Agent.


If you prefer assistant-led setup, the verified[Quickchat AI ChatGPT app](https://quickchat.ai/chatgpt) and[Claude integration](https://quickchat.ai/claude) explain the account connection. Give your assistant the kit and ask it to configure the four Actions, preserve the fixed board and spreadsheet, and leave saving inactive until you finish Google consent and review the settings.


Your finish line is one role with a reason, a tradeoff and a link you can trust enough to investigate. Repeat the search when you want to check the employer again; the shortlist keeps the context you would otherwise have to reconstruct.


## Frequently asked questions


### Can an AI job search assistant search every company?


This build searches the public Greenhouse boards you configure. It starts with Monzo and checks when you ask. It does not search every employer, LinkedIn or private applicant-tracking systems.


### Do I need a Greenhouse API key?


No. Greenhouse’s public Job Board GET endpoints allow unauthenticated reads of published jobs. This tutorial uses the list and job-detail endpoints. Submitting applications is a separate capability and is not configured here.


### Is this a Google Sheets job application tracker?


It starts as a shortlist of roles you choose to investigate. Each row contains the company, job ID, original URL, location, match note and saved status. Change the status yourself after you apply; saving a row does not submit an application.


### Can I use an existing Google Sheet?


Follow this recipe with the spreadsheet created by Quickchat AI’s Google Sheets connection. The connection uses per-file access and does not grant unrestricted access to Drive. Pasting an arbitrary existing spreadsheet ID into an Action does not grant permission to that file.


### Does remote mean I can work from any country?


No. Read the posting’s explicit location and remote-work conditions. Remote (UK) supports working remotely within the UK, not automatic eligibility from another country. When the posting does not answer a location question, the assistant should say so.


### Will the assistant apply for jobs or send daily alerts?


No. This recipe checks openings on request and saves roles after confirmation. Apply through the employer’s original link. Scheduled checks and notifications require a separate trigger and delivery workflow.


### Can ChatGPT or Claude help me set this up?


Yes. They can adapt the starter kit’s prompts and HTTP recipes. An authorized Quickchat AI account-management connection can also configure supported Agent settings. Google sign-in and consent remain with the account owner.


### Do I need to write code?


No. You configure four HTTP Actions in Quickchat AI, paste the supplied Main Prompt and add a Shortlist tab to the app-created Google Sheet. The downloadable kit contains the complete field values and a test checklist; it is not an automatic Agent import.
